text.p: One2One, Britain's smallest mobile telephone company jointly-owned by Cable and Wireless and U S West Inc, said on Thursday it had connected a net 80,000 new customers in the second quarter of the year.
One2One, which said it had won 27.4 percent of net gain growth in the industry, added that its customer base reached 700,000 at the end of June.
One2One, which said its share of the UK market for mobile telephones had risen to 9.5 percent from 7.2 percent, is the last of the four cellular operators to report second quarter subscriber figures.
Both the country's purely digital operators have again outrun the more established market leaders -- Vodafone Group Plc and Cellnet, which is majority-owned by British Telecommunications Plc.

But Orange Plc, the country's youngest mobile telephone group, has been confirmed the winner in the April to June quarter. It added 86,000 net new subscribers in the quarter compared to Cellnet's 74,000 and Vodafone's 53,000.
One2One, which now covers 85 percent of the population, was expected to have reaped the benefit of new tariffs which undercut similar offerings from its rivals.
But some analysts warn that prices in Britain's cellular market still remain too high and will have to drop to European levels if industry forecasts of strong subscriber growth are to be met.

Despite recent moves to cut prices, which have left them at the bottom end of the market almost a third lower than in April, they remain more than 30 percent higher than in the high penetration, high-growth countries in Europe, some analysts note.
